Economists measure economic growth using real GDP, which adjusts for price changes by using constant prices (e.g., base year prices) to reflect only quantity changes. Real GDP growth rates, not nominal GDP, are used to avoid inflation distortions. The text explains that real GDP is the sum of value added and reflects changes in output only, while nominal GDP includes both quantity and price changes.
